clue.text: They'll see you through the rest of the night

definitions.text: They'll see you through the rest of the night

parts.words: They'll see you through the rest of the night
parts.note: read as a promise of company for the remaining hours, but 'rest' means sleep: these are the clothes worn in bed all night

explanation.surface: Someone promises to keep you company until dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See you through' sounds like support until morning; the garments literally cover you while you rest at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is put on for sleep and kept on until morning, so it sees the sleeper through the night's rest.

clue.text: Power and superpower once meeting in area around Berlin

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
Russia, at the heart of the Soviet Union, was a Cold War superpower

explanation.surface: Two great powers come together in negotiations near the German capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic kingdom whose capital was Berlin covered the region around that city.

clue.text: Meet, say, about key decision of both Houses of Congress

definitions.text: decision of both Houses of Congress

parts.note: 'meet' sounds like meat, and a joint is a cut of meat, so 'say' flags both the sound and the example
re is Latin-derived 'concerning', a standard crossword abbreviation for about
a key is the list of answers, the solution to a puzzle

explanation.surface: A gathering about a central decision taken by both chambers of the US legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet, say' leads by sound to meat, of which a joint is an example. 'Key' means the answers to a puzzle, not a lock or musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a measure passed by Senate and House together is called a joint resolution.

clue.text: Procession involving me and a doctor

indicators.note: involving here means tangling up, so the letters of me, a and doctor are mixed together

explanation.surface: A parade in which I take part alongside a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' reads as including, but it signals that ME, A and DOCTOR are rearranged into nine new letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of cars travelling together, often escorting a dignitary, is a kind of procession.

clue.text: Worker in South America, one very busy at the present time?

definitions.text: one very busy at the present time?

indicators.note: in places the worker inside the abbreviation for the continent

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: A labourer in Latin America who is rushed off their feet just now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The present time' looks like 'now' but is a pun on presents: Christmas, when Father Christmas is busiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas delivers gifts at Christmas, his busiest season, the time of presents.

clue.text: At least three items in concert in Notts town

parts.words: At least three items in concert
parts.note: works, plural, means two or more pieces of music played at a concert

parts.words: At least three items in concert
parts.note: op is short for opus, one more musical work, making at least three in all

explanation.surface: A concert programme in a Nottinghamshire town features three or more pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: WORKS gives at least two pieces and OP (opus) one more, hence 'at least three'. Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is a market town in the north of Nottinghamshire, England.

clue.text: Joint reported under prohibition — a watch may be kept on it

definitions.text: a watch may be kept on it

parts.note: the wrist is the joint between hand and forearm

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so a word for under prohibition is heard and spelt another way

parts.note: something under prohibition is banned

explanation.surface: A joint said to be outlawed, kept under observation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' turns BANNED into its sound-alike BAND. 'Keep a watch on' sounds like surveillance, but it is a wristwatch worn on the strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap round the lower arm is where a timepiece is commonly worn.

clue.text: Rapidly approach finish of play?

parts.note: a play's run is the period it is staged
up means finished, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: Hurrying towards the end of a theatre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish of play' sounds like the end of a match; read it as a stage show whose season is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up to someone is to approach them quickly on foot.

clue.text: Misuse of lifts, unescorted, could be suicide

indicators.note: misuse means putting to wrong use, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Riding in elevators alone and improperly might prove fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misuse of' signals that LIFTS and UNESCORTED are rearranged; 'could be' tells you the definition is a fair description.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one's own life is destroying oneself, the literal sense of the compound.

clue.text: Woman surprisingly sylph-like after two reducing operations?

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters turn up in an unexpected order
two reducing operations shortens the word like twice, losing its final two letters

explanation.surface: A slender woman looking willowy after a pair of slimming surgeries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operations' sounds surgical, but each one trims a letter from the end of the word; 'surprisingly' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllis is a female first name.

clue.text: Peacekeepers under canvas charge friendly power without meaning to

parts.note: UN peacekeepers serve under the United Nations
camping under canvas means in a tent
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge
a friendly nation in war is an ally

explanation.surface: UN troops camped in tents attack an allied nation by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an attack, but it is the electrical sense, an ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by accident is doing it with no intention behind it.

clue.text: It's a Norse god -and one for the Greeks

parts.note: 'it' means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
Tyr is the Norse god of war

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a Scandinavian deity and its Greek counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is old slang for sex appeal, SA. 'One for the Greeks' means a creature from Greek mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat-legged woodland spirits who follow Dionysus belong to Greek mythology.

clue.text: Opposite point a lad makes

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A boy scores a point in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' looks like scoring, but it signals that POINT A LAD is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Places on directly opposite sides of the globe are said to be at each other's antipodes.

clue.text: Woman, one from Egyptian city

indicators.note: from tells you the letter for one is taken away from the city name

parts.note: Alexandria is the Mediterranean port founded by Alexander the Great
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman who comes from a city in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One from' reads as origin, but it says I (one) is removed from ALEXANDRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra is a female first name.

clue.text: Dumas hero given a grant and resettled

indicators.note: resettled means moved to a new place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A character from Dumas receives a sum of money and moves house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resettled' signals that A GRANT AND is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The young Gascon who joins the Three Musketeers is Alexandre Dumas's protagonist.

clue.text: School subject emergency solved by money from abroad

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school subject
SOS is the international distress call

explanation.surface: A crisis in the gym class is sorted out with foreign cash.
explanation.definitionFit: These are currency units used in Mexico and other Latin American countries, so foreign money to a British reader.

clue.text: Hanoi epic directed in the old country

indicators.note: directed, like a film, means the letters are arranged by someone into a new order

explanation.surface: A grand saga set in Vietnam's capital, filmed in an ancient land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directed' suggests a film-maker, but it signals that HANOI EPIC is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Mediterranean seafaring nation on the coast of the Levant no longer exists.

clue.text: Sergeant major's right to have a cigarette

parts.note: oke is a slang form of OK, meaning all right

explanation.surface: An NCO is permitted a cigarette break.
explanation.walkthrough: OKE is a dictionary variant of OK; 'right' means fine, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette is informally called a smoke.

clue.text: Batsman who's out?

explanation.surface: A cricketer asks which player has been dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like a cricket dismissal, but the second sense is a worker out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The batsman facing the bowling is the one on strike; a worker who has walked out is on strike.

clue.text: Set carrying little weight, once a source of entertainment

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A lightweight set that used to amuse the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' looks like a container, but the two pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet combining radio and record player was a household entertainment from the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Mother joins me on line in silent performance

parts.note: mum is British informal for mother
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A mother and I appear together in a mime.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummers performed traditional plays in dumb show, so mummery is mime.

clue.text: Writing about worker

parts.note: round means around, about
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the link 'concerning', but it gives ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of clear, rounded penmanship is called round hand.

clue.text: Detective Inspector's drunk tot — same again

parts.note: DI is the abbreviation for Detective Inspector

indicators.note: drunk means messed up, so the letters of tot are jumbled

explanation.surface: A police inspector downs a dram and orders another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as swallowed, but it is the anagram signal for the little dram.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'ditto' means the same thing repeated, as when ordering another of the same drink.

clue.text: Society girl takes little time to get out of service

indicators.note: takes means the society girl holds the time inside her

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a girl entering high society
mo is short for moment, a little time

explanation.surface: A debutante pauses briefly before leaving the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be demobilised is to be released from the armed forces.

clue.text: Police station mostly equipped with American sound system

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the nick is British slang for a police station

explanation.surface: A police station is fitted out with American audio gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is British slang for a police station (and for prison).
explanation.definitionFit: NICAM is a digital stereo standard for television audio.

clue.text: Thin magnetic ink spilled up

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Thin magnetic ink spilled up (8,7)': THIN MAGNETIC INK is anagram fodder and 'spilled' its indicator, but no word is left to define the answer ('up' cannot); the definition seems cut off, and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Denigrate cricket score by county

parts.note: a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket
Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Belittling a cricket total made by a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of Northern Ireland's six counties.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something down is to criticise it disparagingly.

clue.text: glib talk

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'glib talk (7)': only a definition survives, with no wordplay; the clue appears cut short and no reprint was found.
